name: bayes medical test
learning_objective: Teach Bayes theorem for medical test interpretation.

content_set.title: Bayes medical testing note
content_set.text: Bayes theorem connects base rate, sensitivity, specificity, and posterior probability. In medical testing, sensitivity is the true positive rate and specificity is the true negative rate. A positive test result can still have low posterior probability when the disease base rate is low because false positives dominate.

name: convex lens ray optics
learning_objective: Understand convex lens image formation with ray diagrams and solve CBSE/JEE lens formula questions.

content_set.title: Convex lens ray notes
content_set.text: For a convex lens, draw the principal axis, optical center, focal points F1 and F2, and 2F marks. A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through focus after refraction. A ray through the optical center goes straight. The lens formula is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u and magnification is v/u.

name: galvanic cell nernst
learning_objective: Understand galvanic cells, electrode potential, and the Nernst equation for CBSE/JEE electrochemistry.

content_set.title: Electrochemistry note
content_set.text: A galvanic cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Oxidation happens at the anode and reduction happens at the cathode. Electrons flow from anode to cathode through the wire while the salt bridge maintains charge balance. Cell potential is Ecell = Ecathode - Eanode. The Nernst equation adjusts Ecell using the reaction quotient.

name: unseen technical domain transformer attention
learning_objective: Teach transformer attention and KV cache for faster LLM inference.

content_set.title: Attention cache notes
content_set.text: Transformer attention compares query vectors with key vectors to produce attention weights over value vectors. A KV cache stores past key and value tensors during autoregressive decoding, so the model does not recompute attention states for previous tokens. The tradeoff is extra memory usage for lower inference latency.

name: adversarial technical domain linux containers
learning_objective: Explain Linux containers, namespaces, cgroups, and container isolation.

content_set.title: Linux container note
content_set.text: Linux containers isolate processes using namespaces for PID, network, mount, IPC, and users. Cgroups limit CPU, memory, and IO usage for a group of processes. Container images are built from read-only layers plus a writable container layer. Containers share the host kernel, so they are lighter than virtual machines but require careful isolation.

name: heldout payments idempotency keys
learning_objective: Teach backend engineers API idempotency keys, retries, and duplicate charge prevention.

content_set.title: Payments idempotency note
content_set.text: An idempotency key lets a client retry a payment request without creating a duplicate charge. The server stores the key with the first result and returns the same result for later retries. A retry without an idempotency key can double charge a customer when the first response times out after the charge succeeded.

name: heldout backend domain http caching
learning_objective: Teach backend engineers HTTP caching with ETag and Cache-Control for API responses.

content_set.title: HTTP caching note
content_set.text: HTTP caching uses Cache-Control directives such as max-age, no-store, private, and must-revalidate. An ETag is a validator representing a resource version. Clients send If-None-Match with a previous ETag and the server can return 304 Not Modified without the response body. Avoid caching personalized API responses without private or no-store because shared caches can leak user data.
